title: The World Fiscal Uncertainty Index
text: The World Fiscal Uncertainty index (WFU) is the share of all web news articles processed by GDELT worldwide, in English and in approximately 65 machine-translated languages, that carry at the same time an uncertainty term, an economy term and a fiscal term (taxation, government spending, budgets, deficits or public debt). The share is scaled so that its 2016–2025 average equals 100; a value of 200 indicates that such articles were twice as frequent as on average over the decade. Each article enters the world index once, and the world index is not shrunk (see Methodology).

title: Methodology
text: The indices follow the newspaper-based approach of Baker, Bloom and Davis (2016), with two changes. The policy term list is replaced by a fiscal one, so that the index counts articles about taxes, budgets, government spending, deficits and public debt rather than about policy in general. And the fixed set of national newspapers is replaced by the GDELT Global Knowledge Graph, so that one dictionary and one procedure produce comparable indices for about 200 economies — from each economy’s own press and from the press of other countries writing about it. The full treatment is Appendix B of the paper.

title: Methodology
text:
1. The corpus

Every web news article processed by GDELT from 1 January 2016 to 30 September 2026: 1,649,845,652 articles, of which 39 percent are in English and 61 percent are machine-translated from 63 other languages.
GDELT tags each article with themes from a fixed vocabulary that includes the Baker–Bloom–Davis term lists, applied to the translated text with one dictionary. Articles are therefore classified by their theme tags; no keyword list per language is needed.
The sample starts in 2016 because GDELT began applying the Baker–Bloom–Davis tags on 14 December 2015. The base period for scaling is 2016–2025.

\mathrm{FU}_a = U_a\,E_a\,F_a .

title: Methodology
text:
4. From counts to shares
For each view and period, N is the number of articles and K the number of fiscal uncertainty articles among them. The share is a ratio of sums over the period (days, weeks, months, quarters or years), so that periods are weighted by their volume of news:

\hat\pi_{ct} = \frac{K_{ct}}{N_{ct}} .

Fiscal policy uncertainty articles are rare: about 2.2 per 1,000 articles, against 4.4 per 1,000 for economic policy uncertainty. For a small economy the raw share is a few articles divided by a few thousand, and its sampling variation is then of the same order as the variation the index is intended to measure.

title: Methodology
text:
5. Shrinkage (country series)
Following Efron and Morris (1975), the share is treated as a draw from a beta-binomial model centred on the economy’s own 2016–2025 pooled share \bar\pi_c, and replaced by its posterior mean

\tilde\pi_{ct} = \frac{K_{ct}+\kappa\,\bar\pi_{c}}{N_{ct}+\kappa},

where the prior precision \kappa (in articles) is estimated once per series by the method of moments. For the headline annual domestic series \hat\kappa = 488 articles: shrinkage is negligible for large economies and damps only the year-to-year noise of thin ones. Shrinking toward the economy’s own mean, not the cross-country mean, keeps the cross-country differences in level and does not manufacture comovement with the world series. World series are not shrunk.

title: Methodology
text:
6. Scaling

\mathrm{FU}_{ct} = 100\,\frac{\tilde\pi_{ct}}{\overline{\tilde\pi}_{c}},
\qquad
\mathrm{FU\_Z}_{ct} = \frac{\ln\tilde\pi_{ct}-\mu_{c}}{\sigma_{c}},

where \overline{\tilde\pi}_{c}, \mu_c and \sigma_c are the 2016–2025 mean of the share and the mean and standard deviation of its logarithm, within each economy and at each frequency. The index (e.g. DFU) equals 100 on average over 2016–2025 in every economy and is the form for figures; the z-score (e.g. DFU_Z) is the form for regressions. The narrative gap is FUGAP_Z = XFU_Z − DFU_Z.
Flags. A cell is thin when the view has fewer than 1,000 articles or 10 fiscal uncertainty articles in a month (1,500 and 15 in a quarter; 2,000 and 20 in a year). COMPBRK flags cells where the all-outlet and stable-panel indices differ by more than a factor of two, a sign of a change in outlet composition.
Timing. Annual files also give the domestic, foreign and all-sources indices on the IMF WEO fiscal-year basis (_FY) and for the six pre-budget months before the fiscal year starts (_PB), labelled with the WEO fiscal year.

title: Data
text:
Notes on use

In regression analysis the standardized series (*_Z) are recommended: one unit is one within-economy standard deviation of the log share, which makes coefficients comparable across economies whose press differs in size.
The indices (2016–2025 mean = 100 in every economy) are intended for figures.
Comparisons of levels across economies should use the shares (*_SH).
Thin cells (THIN_D = 1) should be excluded or down-weighted, and the stable-panel series DFU_PNL used where COMPBRK_D = 1.

title: World Fiscal Uncertainty
text:
This site distributes the fiscal policy uncertainty indices constructed in Balcilar (2026), Global Uncertainty and Fiscal Space: Who Can Still Afford to Act? (PDF). The indices measure the frequency of news articles that discuss taxation, government spending, budget deficits or public debt together with uncertainty about the economy. They are computed from the Global Knowledge Graph of the GDELT Project, which records approximately 1.65 billion web news articles in English and some 65 other languages published between 1 January 2016 and 30 September 2026.
The world index is available at daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual frequency. Country indices are available for 245 economies at monthly, quarterly and annual frequency, measured separately in the domestic press of each economy, in the foreign press writing about it, and in all sources that mention it.

title: Variable definitions
text:
Variable names are built from three parts: view + measure + variant, followed by a suffix for the scale.


View (first letter)

W world
D domestic press
X foreign press
A all sources



Measure

FU fiscal uncertainty
FA fiscal attention
EPU economic policy unc.
MPU, TPU monetary, trade
SDU sovereign-debt unc.
UNC any uncertainty



Suffix (scale)

none index, 2016–2025 = 100
_Z standardized log share
_SH share per 1,000 articles



Variant tags sit between the measure and the scale suffix: lexicon _UB, _EB, _FN, _FB; construction _NOE, _FOC, _INT; sample _PNL, _NAT, _OWN, _ENG; timing _FY, _PB. For example, DFU_FB_Z is the standardized domestic fiscal uncertainty with the broad fiscal lexicon, and XEPU_PNL is the foreign-press economic policy uncertainty index on the stable outlet panel.
The column Files shows where each variable appears: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annual.
